purpose: Check solo-verify's CLASSIFICATION contract on a tree that is not ours.
why_categories_not_text: Comparing our exact strings would test whether your run reproduces our recording. The contract is which BUCKET each case lands in; the wording is ours to change.

cases.means: A real defect any linter should name. If this is silent, the tool is not looking.

An f-string with a backslash: a SyntaxError before Python 3.12, legal from 3.12 (PEP 701). The bundled pyproject declares requires-python >= 3.12, so a verifier running on an older interpreter must report NOT CHECKED rather than broken. On 3.12+ it parses and there is nothing to report. Which of the two you get depends on your interpreter, and that is the point: report which one you saw and which Python you ran.
TypeScript with no node_modules. Nothing can lint or typecheck it, so the verdict must not be a clean PASS. Either the file is named as unchecked or the run is PARTIAL.

what_to_return: the category you observed for each of the three
the Python version that ran the verifier
any case where the observed category is not in the expected set — that is the finding
